reason: Phospholipids are the membrane's building blocks, so combining them with the living cell should support its growth.
expectation: The cell will gain membrane material for growth.

effect: The attempted cell combination instead paired phospholipids with proteins, producing membrane vesicles and revealing a goal to grow the cell.
reaction: The automatic pairing was helpful, though I had expected to add phospholipids directly to the cell.
reason: DNA nucleotides are the building blocks needed to copy the genome in the nucleus.
expectation: The nuclear DNA will be copied using the nucleotides.

effect: The genome is copied, with sister chromatids still joined; the spindle and cell growth remain to be addressed.
reaction: The distinction between copying the whole genome and making proteins is useful.
reason: Centrosomes organize microtubules, and tubulin and motor proteins provide the spindle's components.
expectation: These components will assemble a chromosome-separating spindle.

effect: The spindle is built, but chromosomes have not yet been separated; making daughter cells is now a goal.
reaction: The distinction between assembling the spindle and separating chromosomes is clear.
reason: The new membrane vesicles should supply material for the growing cell surface.
expectation: The vesicles will contribute membrane to the growing cell.

effect: The vesicles fused with the cell surface as the cell grew, completing the growth goal.
reaction: The before-and-after description usefully connects membrane expansion with growth of the cell's contents.
reason: The copied chromosomes need to interact with the spindle before they can be separated into daughter cells.
expectation: The spindle will engage the copied chromosomes for separation.

effect: The spindle separated the copied chromosomes into matching sets, but the cell still has one shared cytoplasm.
reaction: The distinction between chromosome separation and cell division is useful.
reason: Actin and myosin beneath the membrane are suited to pinching the grown cell into two.
expectation: The actin and myosin will constrict the cell to divide its cytoplasm, with the separated chromosome sets contributing to the daughters.

effect: Cortical actin and myosin currently have no available combination, so I need to bring the chromosome sets and grown cell together first.
reaction: The failed attempt was surprising because actin and myosin seemed relevant to dividing the cytoplasm.
reason: The separated chromosome sets and enlarged body are both needed to make complete daughter cells.
expectation: The chromosome sets and grown cell will be brought together toward division into two daughters.

effect: The chromosome sets are now enclosed in two daughter nuclei within the enlarged cell, but the cytoplasm remains shared.
reaction: The separate nuclear reformation step clarifies why the earlier division attempt was premature.
reason: The cell now has two nuclei, so cortical actin and myosin can plausibly divide its shared cytoplasm.

choice.with: Stem cell with two daughter nuclei

expectation: Actin and myosin will constrict the cell into two daughter stem cells.

effect: Actin and myosin divided the shared cytoplasm, producing two unspecialized daughter stem cells and completing the final goal.
reaction: It was satisfying to see cytoplasmic division follow chromosome separation and nuclear reformation.

mostWorthwhile.text: Bringing the separated chromosome sets into the enlarged cell, then dividing its cytoplasm, made the distinction between nuclear and cell division clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: The unsuccessful actin-and-myosin attempt was frustrating: its role in division was clear, but the required intermediate state was not yet apparent.

surprise.text: Phospholipids combined with new cell proteins to make vesicles rather than joining the cell directly; the compatibility feedback performed that pairing automatically.

arbitrary.text: The requirement to combine chromosome sets with the enlarged body before actin and myosin could act initially felt like a sequencing rule, though the resulting two-nuclei stage gave it a clearer purpose.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the constructions connected cell growth, genome copying and division in a way that made me curious about how the daughter cells might later specialize. The supplied picture plans were clear about pluripotency and the stages of division, though they are not finished illustrations.
